trial_court: 7 th Judicial Magistrate, First Class, Kalol in Criminal Case No.2272 of 2014
case_name: Rao Maheshkumar Govindbhai vs State Of Gujarat
facts_of_case: The respondent No. 2 came upfront before the appellant to sell his house and the deal was made for 4,00,000/- The appellant lend the below amount by cheques. The respondent No.2 gave a cheque of Rs. 4,00,000/- to clear the debt. The said cheque given by the respondent No.2 was presented in Bank of India by the appellant and the same was bounced.

legal_principles.principle: The accused has to rebut the statutory presumption in favour of the holder.
legal_principles.held: The accused failed to rebut the statutory presumption as per section 139 of the Negotiable Instruments Act.
cited_cases: R. Mohan Vs. A.K. Vijaya Kumar, (2013) 1 GLR 222

legal_principles.principle: The accused has to bring on record facts and circumstances upon consideration of which the Court may either believe that the consideration did not exist or its non-existence was so probable that a prudent man would act upon the plea.
legal_principles.held: Once it is admitted by the accused that the cheque is signed by the accused, the accused has to bring on record facts and circumstances...

outcome.final_order: The trial court's judgment acquitting the private respondent No. 2 - original accused from the offence punishable under sections 138 of Negotiable Instrument Act is set aside and the case is remanded to the trial court for fresh disposal.

use_for_drafting: drafting an appeal against conviction in cheque bounce cases
